conceptCapsule.title: Unit Conversion Between Different Physical Systems
conceptCapsule.summary: A physical quantity remains invariant under changes of measurement systems: $Q = n_1 u_1 = n_2 u_2$. When transforming a dimensional quantity $[M^a L^b T^c]$ to a new system with custom base scales, the numerical value transforms inversely proportional to the ratio of base units.
conceptCapsule.examTrap: Supplementary units like plane angle (radian) and solid angle (steradian) have defined units in SI but are strictly dimensionless ($[M^0 L^0 T^0]$). Also remember that Coulomb is a derived unit ($A \cdot s$), while Ampere is the fundamental SI base unit.

questions.statement: Which of the following sets represents quantities that are all fundamental base quantities in the International System of Units (SI)?

options.text: Mass, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance
Electric charge, time, mass, luminous intensity

questions.solution:
The 7 SI fundamental base quantities are: Length (m), Mass (kg), Time (s), Electric Current (A), Thermodynamic Temperature (K), Amount of Substance (mol), and Luminous Intensity (cd).
Velocity, force, and electric charge ($Q=It$) are derived quantities.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In the CGS system, the unit of force is the dyne. The ratio of $1\text{ N}$ (SI unit of force) to $1\text{ dyne}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
1. $\text{Force} = \text{Mass} \times \text{Acceleration}$
2. In SI: $1\text{ N} = 1\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$
3. In CGS: $1\text{ dyne} = 1\text{ g}\cdot\text{cm}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$
4. Converting SI to CGS: $$1\text{ N} = (10^3\text{ g}) \times (10^2\text{ cm}) \times \text{s}^{-2} = 10^5\text{ dyne}$$ Thus, $\frac{1\text{ N}}{1\text{ dyne}} = 10^5$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The FPS system of units uses Foot, Pound, and Second. Given that $1\text{ foot} = 30.48\text{ cm}$ and $1\text{ pound (mass)} \approx 453.6\text{ g}$, the value of $1\text{ slug}$ (the standard FPS unit of mass defined as $1\text{ lbf}\cdot\text{s}^2/\text{ft}$) in SI units ($\text{kg}$) is approximately:
questions.solution:
By definition in the FPS engineering gravitational/derived system, a slug is the mass that accelerates at $1\text{ ft}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$ under a force of $1\text{ lbf}$ ($32.174\text{ lb mass}$):
$$1\text{ slug} = 32.174\text{ lb} \approx 32.174 \times 0.45359\text{ kg} \approx 14.59\text{ kg}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: In the SI system, plane angle and solid angle are:

options.text: Supplementary/dimensionless derived quantities having units (radian and steradian)

questions.solution:
Plane angle ($\theta = l/r$, unit: radian) and solid angle ($\Omega = A/r^2$, unit: steradian) are ratios of identical physical dimensions (length/length or area/area), making them dimensionless, yet they possess distinct supplementary units in SI.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: The SI unit of surface tension is $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}$. In the CGS system, its unit is $\text{dyne}\cdot\text{cm}^{-1}$. A value of $0.072\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}$ in the CGS system is:
questions.solution:
1. Surface tension $T = \frac{F}{L}$
2. $1\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^{-1} = \frac{10^5\text{ dyne}}{10^2\text{ cm}} = 10^3\text{ dyne}\cdot\text{cm}^{-1}$
3. Therefore: $$0.072\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^{-1} = 0.072 \times 10^3 = 72\text{ dyne}\cdot\text{cm}^{-1}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: Which of the following is NOT a base unit in the SI system?
questions.solution:
Coulomb (C) is a derived unit of electric charge defined as current multiplied by time ($1\text{ C} = 1\text{ A}\cdot\text{s}$). The base SI unit for electrical quantities is Ampere (A).
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: The universal gravitational constant $G$ in SI units is $6.67\times 10^{-11}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{kg}^{-2}$. Its numerical value in CGS units ($\text{dyne}\cdot\text{cm}^2\cdot\text{g}^{-2}$) is:
questions.solution:
Dimensions of $G$ are $[M^{-1} L^3 T^{-2}]$.
Using unit conversion: $$n_2 = n_1 \left(\frac{M_1}{M_2}\right)^{-1} \left(\frac{L_1}{L_2}\right)^3 \left(\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^{-2}$$ $$n_2 = 6.67\times 10^{-11} \times \left(\frac{1000\text{ g}}{1\text{ g}}\right)^{-1} \times \left(\frac{100\text{ cm}}{1\text{ cm}}\right)^3 = 6.67\times 10^{-11} \times 10^{-3} \times 10^6 = 6.67\times 10^{-8}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The SI unit of dynamic viscosity $\eta$ is $\text{Pa}\cdot\text{s}$ ($\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$), whereas its CGS unit is poise ($\text{g}\cdot\text{cm}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$). $1\text{ Pa}\cdot\text{s}$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
1. In SI: $1\text{ Pa}\cdot\text{s} = 1\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$
2. Converting to CGS: $$1\text{ Pa}\cdot\text{s} = \frac{1000\text{ g}}{(100\text{ cm})\cdot\text{s}} = 10\text{ g}\cdot\text{cm}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} = 10\text{ poise}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: If a new system of units is chosen where the unit of mass is $2\text{ kg}$, the unit of length is $5\text{ m}$, and the unit of time is $10\text{ s}$, then $1\text{ Joule}$ of energy in this new system is equal to:
questions.solution:
Dimensions of Energy are $[M^1 L^2 T^{-2}]$.
$$n_2 = n_1 \left(\frac{M_1}{M_2}\right)^1 \left(\frac{L_1}{L_2}\right)^2 \left(\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^{-2}$$ $$n_2 = 1 \times \left(\frac{1\text{ kg}}{2\text{ kg}}\right)^1 \times \left(\frac{1\text{ m}}{5\text{ m}}\right)^2 \times \left(\frac{1\text{ s}}{10\text{ s}}\right)^{-2} = 1 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{25} \times 100 = 2\text{ new units}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Which of the following derived units is correctly expressed purely in terms of SI fundamental units?
questions.solution:
1. $\text{Watt} = \frac{\text{Work}}{\text{Time}} = \frac{\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-2}}{\text{s}} = \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-3}$ (Correct)
2. $\text{Pascal} = \frac{F}{A} = \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$
3. $\text{Volt} = \frac{W}{Q} = \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-3}\cdot\text{A}^{-1}$
4. $\text{Tesla} = \frac{F}{I L} = \text{kg}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}\cdot\text{A}^{-1}$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The density of a liquid is $13.6\text{ g}\cdot\text{cm}^{-3}$ in CGS units. In a new system of units where the unit of mass is $100\text{ g}$ and the unit of length is $10\text{ cm}$, the numerical value of the density is:
questions.solution:
Dimensions of Density are $[M^1 L^{-3}]$.
$$n_2 = n_1 \left(\frac{M_1}{M_2}\right)^1 \left(\frac{L_1}{L_2}\right)^{-3}$$ $$n_2 = 13.6 \times \left(\frac{1\text{ g}}{100\text{ g}}\right)^1 \times \left(\frac{1\text{ cm}}{10\text{ cm}}\right)^{-3} = 13.6 \times \frac{1}{100} \times 1000 = 136$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The heat capacity of a substance in SI units is expressed in $\text{J}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}$. In terms of fundamental SI base units, it is written as:
questions.solution:
Heat capacity $C = \frac{Q}{\Delta T}$.
Since Joule (energy) $= \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$, dividing by temperature in Kelvin ($\text{K}$) gives: $$[C] = \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-2}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In a system where the unit of force is $100\text{ N}$, the unit of length is $10\text{ m}$, and the unit of time is $100\text{ s}$, the unit of mass in this system corresponds to:
questions.solution:
Since Force $F = M L T^{-2}$, we can isolate Mass $M$:
$$M = \frac{F T^2}{L}$$ Substituting values: $$M = \frac{100\text{ N} \times (100\text{ s})^2}{10\text{ m}} = \frac{100 \times 10000}{10} = 10^5\text{ kg}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: Which of the following physical quantities has a derived unit that is dimensionless in SI?
questions.solution:
Specific gravity is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of pure water at $4^\circ\text{C}$. Being a pure ratio of two identical physical dimensions, it has no units and is dimensionless ($[M^0 L^0 T^0]$).
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In the CGS electrostatic unit (esu) system, the unit of electric charge is the statcoulomb. How many statcoulombs are there in $1\text{ Coulomb}$ of charge?
questions.solution:
From electrostatics conversions between SI and CGS-esu:
$$1\text{ Coulomb} = 3\times 10^9\text{ statcoulomb (or esu of charge)}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the Ohm ($\Omega$). Expressed entirely in base units ($\text{kg, m, s, A}$), $1\ \Omega$ is equivalent to:
questions.solution:
Resistance $R = \frac{V}{I} = \frac{\text{Power}}{I^2} = \frac{\text{Work}}{\text{Time}\cdot I^2}$.
Expressing in base units: $$1\ \Omega = \frac{\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-2}}{\text{s}\cdot\text{A}^2} = \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-3}\cdot\text{A}^{-2}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The value of acceleration due to gravity is $g = 9.8\text{ m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$. If the unit of length is chosen to be $1\text{ km}$ and the unit of time is $1\text{ minute}$, the numerical value of $g$ in this new system will be:
questions.solution:
Acceleration has dimensions $[L^1 T^{-2}]$.
Here $L_1 = 1\text{ m}$, $T_1 = 1\text{ s}$, $L_2 = 1000\text{ m}$, $T_2 = 60\text{ s}$.
$$n_2 = 9.8 \times \left(\frac{1\text{ m}}{1000\text{ m}}\right)^1 \times \left(\frac{1\text{ s}}{60\text{ s}}\right)^{-2} = 9.8 \times \frac{3600}{1000} = 9.8 \times 3.6 = 35.28$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The SI unit of inductance is Henry (H). Which of the following combinations of base units correctly represents $1\text{ H}$?
questions.solution:
Magnetic energy stored in an inductor is $U = \frac{1}{2} L I^2 \implies L = \frac{2U}{I^2}$.
Units of energy $= \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$.
Dividing by $\text{A}^2$: $$1\text{ H} = \text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-2}\cdot\text{A}^{-2}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The work done in moving a body is $10\text{ J}$ in MKS/SI. If work is to be converted into CGS (erg), $10\text{ J}$ corresponds to:
questions.solution:
1. In SI: $1\text{ J} = 1\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-2}$
2. Converting to CGS: $1\text{ J} = 10^3\text{ g} \times 10^4\text{ cm}^2 \times \text{s}^{-2} = 10^7\text{ erg}$
3. For $10\text{ J}$: $$10\text{ J} = 10 \times 10^7\text{ erg} = 10^8\text{ erg}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: The Stefan-Boltzmann constant $\sigma$ has the SI unit $\text{W}\cdot\text{m}^{-2}\cdot\text{K}^{-4}$. In terms of SI base fundamental units, it is:
questions.solution:
1. Radiation energy flux $E = \sigma T^4 \implies \sigma = \frac{E}{T^4}$
2. $E$ is power per unit area: $\frac{\text{W}}{\text{m}^2} = \frac{\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-3}}{\text{m}^2} = \text{kg}\cdot\text{s}^{-3}$
3. Dividing by $\text{K}^4$: $$[\sigma] = \text{kg}\cdot\text{s}^{-3}\cdot\text{K}^{-4}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.
